title: A uniform bound for proper direct image
statement:
Use the universe and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]; all filtered diagrams and families are small in its chosen universe. Use the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p_0>0$ with $p_0\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms. The field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]; $\Qlb$ has the condensed coefficient meaning of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Sheaves below are module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] for the pulled-back ring $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for their filtered colimits in the ambient module category, as in clause (2) of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness]. Here $R^qp_*M=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*(M[0]))$, using the module-object derived direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Properness is [def-weil-proper-morphism], geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre], and dimension means the Krull dimension of the underlying topological space [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Let $p\colon X\to Y$ be proper, and let $d$ be an integer bounding the dimensions
of all geometric fibres of $p$ (for instance $d=\dim X$). For $M\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$
([det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness]),

$$
R^qp_*M=0\quad(q>2d+1),\qquad R^qp_*M\in\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)\quad(q\geq0),
$$

and $R^qp_*\colon\IndCons(X,\Lambda)\to\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$ preserves arbitrary direct sums.

The proof computes with an integral lattice. Its reductions modulo $\pi_E^n$ satisfy the classical
torsion bound $2d$, and the derived inverse limit over $n$ costs one more degree, whence $2d+1$.

proof.text: Convert the finite-lower-bound hypothesis on each geometric fibre to topologicalKrullDim <= bottom when d<0 and <= d.toNat otherwise. Split WithBot and ENat into bottom, finite and top. Bottom is automatic; the finite case follows by testing its own dimension, and top is ruled out by testing d.toNat+1. Apply the two coefficient cases of det-proper-heart-bound-rational, converting CharP k p0 to ringChar k=p0. This supplies constructible vanishing above 2d+1.

Use lem-proper-heart-constructible-cohomology to obtain finite constant-model constructibility of every nonnegative higher direct image of a constructible input. This isolates the constant-model issue, without a dimension bound, continuity or ind-objects.

Properness supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. For a small filtered diagram M use the strict diagram M[0]. Good truncation at zero is an isomorphism on each term, so precomposing the truncated-colimit cocone by that isomorphism gives a colimit cocone of M[0]. The actual internal-module continuity theorem lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity makes its mapped cocone colimiting. The single-complex functor preserves colimits. Thus its composite with derived pushforward and degree-q homology preserves filtered colimits. This bypasses the sectionwise-module comparison.

Unpack ObjectProperty.ind to present M as a small filtered colimit of finite constant-model constructibles. Map its presentation by the higher direct-image functor. Preservation from the previous step makes the mapped cocone colimiting. Its terms vanish above 2d+1, so its vertex is zero. In nonnegative degrees its terms are constructible by the second step, so the mapped presentation witnesses membership of ObjectProperty.ind on Y.

The higher direct-image functor is additive. Its preservation of filtered colimits therefore implies preservation of arbitrary coproducts by the existing finite-subcoproduct theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_of_preservesColimitsOfShape_finset. Apply isColimitOfPreserves to the specified cofan, retaining its original legs. The empty family is included. This proves exactly the asserted coproduct universal property.

I read the item, all 34 cited statements, the unit record, the main-20261015 blueprint unit and proof, and the Stacks sources 01T6, 070J, 015Z, 03DA/03DB, 095U and 09A6. The statement is word for word the blueprint's: Λ=E or Q̄_ℓ, p proper, fibre bound d, vanishing for q>2d+1, R^q p_* in IndCons, and preservation of direct sums. Edge cases hold: d<0 forces X empty, d=0 gives an upper bound only, q=2d+1 is not claimed, and the empty sum is fine. Step 1: qcqs follows from the proper, finite-type, closed-immersion and affine-qcqs nodes. X and Y are Noetherian by Stacks 01T6, as det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness requires. Step 2 uses only the statement of the same-unit node det-proper-heart-bound-rational. Step 3 uses clause (2) of det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational, the blueprint's own step-6 input. I accept that tool use and found no DAG cycle in the full transitive closure. Steps 4–5 correctly identify internal Λ_X-modules with the sectionwise A-modules of det-proper-heart-continuity-direct-image. They use the internal/sectionwise equivalence, which is the identity on underlying sheaves, injective-resolution transport, bounded-below injective complexes being K-injective (Stacks 070J), and the exact, colimit-preserving forgetful functor. Restriction along Λ_Y→p_*Λ_X is handled, and naturality comes from transported lifts. Steps 6–7 apply clause (2) of the ind-heart node, the continuity clauses and closure under sums, with the coproduct in the full subcategory written out. Accepted tool uses: det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational, lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution, lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful; the ind-heart and continuity nodes are on the unit route. There are no new nodes. The duplicate det-proper-heart-bound-indcons is correctly in same_as and not used as a dependency. Maintainer notes: source.external still lists Stacks 0991, which is the proetale-section-points tag; the right inputs are 0946/098H, and the proof does not use 0991. lean.statement: theorem properHeartBound (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ) (k : Type u) [Field k] (p₀ : ℕ) [CharP k p₀] (hp₀ : 0 < p₀) (hpℓ : p₀ ≠ ℓ) (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] (p : X ⟶ Y) [p.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper p] (d : ℤ) (hd : ∀ (y : Y) (n : ℕ), (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim (pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (Y.residueField y) (AlgebraicClosure (Y.residueField y)))) ≫ Y.fromSpecResidueField y) : Scheme.{u}) → (n : ℤ) ≤ d) : ProperHeartBoundAssertions (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} E) p d
lean.note: The two theorems state the finite E and condensed algebraic-closure cases. The real-data helpers expand the canonical degree-zero derived direct image and the three assertions. The integer fibre bound is tested against every finite lower bound of topologicalKrullDim, preserving negative d and empty fibres. Direct-sum preservation is stated by images of arbitrary ambient colimit cofans of ind-constructibles, equivalently sums in the full replete IndCons categories.
